item.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Fed Minutes in Focus as Near-Term Rate-Hike Prospects Dim
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve’s minutes for its September meeting are due Wednesday and will mark the highlight of the coming week.

item.title: Average 30-year mortgage rates hit 7.03% this week, the first time they have surpassed 7% since the beginning of last year
item.content:encoded: The effect of rates topping the psychologically important 7% level is rippling through the market for buyers, sellers and builders.

item.title: KB Home Cuts Margin Outlook as Housing Conditions Worsen
item.content:encoded: The homebuilder said it now expects annual gross profit margin to be 16.0% to 16.2%, down from its earlier guidance of 16.1% to 16.5%.

item.title: Many people who are willing to move a little further from the city, or buy a smaller home, are figuring out that it is still possible to buy
item.content:encoded: A tour of a neighborhood near Seattle shows how a younger generation is making it work in one of the least affordable housing markets in decades.

item.title: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said officials may need more time before deciding whether to raise interest rates again, echoing signals from another Fed leader this week that cast doubt on bets the central bank would lift rates at its meeting later this month
item.content:encoded: Vice Chair Jefferson echoes another central bank official who cast doubt on an October hike.

item.title: Fed’s Kashkari Says Inflation Still Too High, Latest Data Didn’t Change View
item.content:encoded: Kashkari said the bigger surprise in the latest batch of inflation data was the revisions to gross domestic product growth that suggested a resilient economy and consumer.

item.title: Treasury Yields Hit Fresh Highs
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury yields reversed early declines and the bonds selloff resumed as an uncertain long-term outlook offset temporary inflation relief.

item.title: New York Fed President John Williams said that the Federal Reserve needn’t rush to continue raising interest rates after officials voted through the first rate increase in three years last week
item.content:encoded: The remarks could reset expectations for the central bank’s next move at a meeting four weeks away.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Ticked Lower in September
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index landed at 48.1 in September, down from 51.7 in August.

item.title: German Consumer Confidence Falls to Lowest Since May on Energy Costs
item.content:encoded: Consumer confidence in Germany dropped unexpectedly sharply, dragged down by rising energy prices as tensions escalated in the Middle East.

item.title: The U.S. added 29,000 jobs in September, far short of expectations, in a sign that the labor market remains steady but may not be able to deliver consistent and sizable employment gains
item.content:encoded: Anemic hiring fell far short of expectations with 29,000 jobs added last month, but the unemployment rate remains near historic lows.

item.title: Dollar Falls After Weak U.S. Jobs Data, Boosting Swiss Franc Further
item.content:encoded: The U.S. dollar fell after weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data dampened expectations for another interest-rate rise by the Federal Reserve later this month.

item.title: Eurozone Inflation Jumps to Three-Year High on Sharper Energy Costs
item.content:encoded: Consumer prices were 3.8% higher in September than the same month of last year, up from 3.2% in August.

item.title: Heard on the Street: High government debt is adding fuel to the global bond market selloff
item.content:encoded: Oil prices are driving rates higher, but indebtedness is a key risk factor.

item.title: Is it plausible that Americans will spend as much of their income on artificial intelligence as they do on food, asks @greg_ip
item.content:encoded: To justify staggering investment sums, Americans will have to spend as much of their income on this one technology as they do on food.

item.title: Global Economy Stronger Than Expected, But Threats Mount, OECD Says
item.content:encoded: A lengthy conflict in the Middle East in combination with other headwinds could take a big toll on activity around the world, the Paris-based research body said.

item.title: Eurozone Economy Surged as War Ignited Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: The bloc’s GDP picked up more rapidly than previously estimated in the quarter through June, but that resilience will be tested if the Iran war continues to block the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: El Nino Is Yet to Peak, Bringing Heat and Agricultural Damage in Tow, UN Says
item.content:encoded: This year’s El Nino is on track to be the strongest in at least 70 years, further increasing the likelihood of widescale disruption to global agricultural markets.

item.title: Mortgage rates posted their largest increase in four years this week
item.content:encoded: The rise to 7.28% follows the bond-market rout and deals another blow to a limping housing market.

item.title: U.S. Home Price Growth Increases Again
item.content:encoded: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index, which measures home prices across the country, rose 1.9% in the 12 months through July, compared with a 1.6% increase in June.
